outcome: No proof, disproof, or partial case-settlement of the stated conjecture (closed aspherical manifolds determined up to homeomorphism by their fundamental group) was found in the window; the closest results are about two related-but-distinct statements, neither of which is a restriction of the stated question.
summary: I could not find any result in the window (26 Jan 2024 – 22 Sep 2026) that resolves, partially resolves, or moves a bound on the stated conjecture: that closed aspherical manifolds are determined up to homeomorphism by their fundamental groups. The triage's lead, Davis & Hillman, 'The Borel Conjecture for manifolds with boundary' (arXiv:2501.12509, v1 21 Jan 2025, revised through v2 29 Jun 2026), proves a case of a *different* conjecture: the 'Borel Conjecture for manifolds with boundary' asks whether a homotopy equivalence of compact aspherical manifolds-with-boundary that is already a homeomorphism on the boundary is homotopic rel boundary to a homeomorphism — a statement posed for a different class of objects (manifolds with nonempty boundary) with an extra boundary hypothesis, not obtainable by simply restricting the closed-manifold statement in our bullet. Per Manifold Atlas and the paper's own framing, this is the standard related-but-distinct 'Borel Conjecture for manifolds with boundary,' developed in analogy with the closed case rather than as a special case of it. I also found a second candidate, Davis, Hayden, Huang, Ruberman & Sunukjian, 'Exotic aspherical 4-manifolds' (arXiv:2411.19400, v1 28 Nov 2024, v3 5 May 2026), which constructs closed, aspherical, smooth 4-manifolds that are homeomorphic but not diffeomorphic — a counterexample to the *smooth* analogue of Borel (diffeomorphism, not homeomorphism), which Wikipedia's own article already records as false (with the smooth-vs-topological distinction stated explicitly in the encyclopedia's wording of the conjecture we were given: 'This conjecture is false if topological manifolds and homeomorphisms are replaced by smooth manifolds and diffeomorphisms'). Because our stated conjecture is specifically about homeomorphism (the topological, not smooth, category), this result changes nothing about the bullet's status; it is a different statement and, moreover, one whose falsity in a related form was already known/expected before the frozen date. I also checked Lück's 'Survey on the Farrell-Jones Conjecture' (arXiv:2507.11337, 2025, to appear Bull. AMS): it is an expository survey with no new theorems of its own, and it frames the general Full Farrell-Jones Conjecture (whose truth for a torsion-free group implies Borel for that group's manifolds in dim ≥5) as still open, consistent with the general Borel conjecture remaining open. Lück–Macko's 2024 book 'Surgery Theory: Foundations' is likewise an exposition, not new research. The current live Wikipedia article on the Borel conjecture contains no mention of any 2024–2026 development. I found no AI involvement anywhere near this problem: none of the mathematical papers above mention AI assistance, and a tangential hit (an autoformalization-agent paper, 'Aria', arXiv:2510.04520) mentions using 'Borel's Conjecture in topology' only as a benchmark case for testing definition-retrieval in an automated formalization pipeline — it formalizes existing definitions/statements rather than proving or advancing anything, so it is not a mathematical event and not `ai_role` other than none even by inference (no authors' account ties it to a proof). A separate 'Human mathematicians are being outcounterexampled' post (Xena blog, Jul 2026) that surfaced in AI-adjacent searches discusses unrelated conjectures (Erdős unit-distance, a Grothendieck question, the Jacobian conjecture) and does not mention the Borel conjecture at all — a false lead from query overlap, not a finding. I therefore agree with the triage's underlying observation (the Davis-Hillman paper exists and is real) but disagree with treating it as progress on this stated bullet: it is a related problem under §3.1, not a case, so status remains `open` with `no_change_found` true.
competing_reading: One could argue the manifolds-with-boundary Borel conjecture is close enough in spirit — same conjecturer, same techniques (surgery theory, Farrell-Jones), same 'topological rigidity' slogan — that progress there is evidence-adjacent progress on the closed case, and some expositors (e.g., Manifold Atlas, which houses both under overlapping page structures) treat them as a family. If Davis and Hillman's technique is understood to eventually reduce to or imply results for closed manifolds via boundary-capping arguments, a future reader might argue for `partial`/`progress` instead of `open`. I did not find any explicit statement in the papers claiming implications for the closed-manifold case, so I did not adopt this reading.
what_would_settle_it: A published statement, by Davis, Hillman, or another expert, that their manifolds-with-boundary results imply a new case of the closed aspherical manifold Borel conjecture (e.g., via doubling or boundary-capping constructions extending fundamental-group classes for which the closed conjecture is now known); or any new paper directly proving/disproving a case of the closed conjecture within the window.
